## Circular to intermediaries 1 licensed or registered for Type 6 regulated activity

## The new sponsor regime

Following our circular and press release dated 15 December 2006, we would like to update the industry on the implementation of the new sponsor regulatory regime, which will become effective on 1 January 2007.

As at 29 December 2006, there are a total of 267 intermediaries 2 licensed or registered for Type  6  regulated  activity.    Of  these  267  intermediaries,  183  have  been  imposed  with  the licensing condition restricting them from acting as sponsors with effect from 1 January 2007 ('Licensing  Condition').    The  Public  Register  on  the  SFC  website  has  been  updated accordingly to reflect the status of these intermediaries.

Intermediaries that cannot act as sponsors

Intermediaries that cannot act as sponsors have been imposed with the Licensing Condition. These intermediaries generally fall into the following categories:

- Intermediaries that have informed the SFC that they do not intend to act as sponsors;
- Intermediaries  that  never  responded  to  the  SFC  regarding  their  intentions.    These intermediaries were issued with Letters of Mindedness ('LOMs') as a result of the nonresponse and did not make any representations in response to the LOMs; and
- Intermediaries  that  have  made  submissions  to  act  as  sponsors,  but  did  not  meet  the eligibility  criteria.    These  intermediaries  were  issued  with  LOMs,  which  set  out  the grounds that led to SFC's view that these intermediaries are not eligible to act as sponsors but the intermediaries did not make any representations in response to the LOMs.

Intermediaries that can act as sponsors

Intermediaries that have met the eligibility criteria prescribed in the Guidelines for Sponsors and  Compliance  Advisers  should  have  by  now  received  a  notification  from  the  SFC

confirming the intermediaries' eligibility as sponsors.  In addition to the confirmation of the intermediaries' eligibility as sponsors, the SFC notification also sets out the individuals that are  eligible  to  act  as  Principals  for  the  sponsors.    In  some  instances,  not  all  individuals nominated by these sponsors were confirmed eligible to act as Principals.

No Licensing Condition will be imposed on these intermediaries, and these intermediaries may act or continue to act as sponsors after 1 January 2007.

## Intermediaries under assessment

Intermediaries  that  have  made  submissions  but  failed  to  demonstrate  that  they  meet  the sponsor eligibility criteria were issued with LOMs.  The LOMs set out the grounds that led to the  SFC's  preliminary  view  that  the  intermediaries  are  not  eligible  to  act  as  sponsors,  and their  appointed  individuals  are  not  eligible  to  act  as  Principals.  These  intermediaries  were given  the  opportunity  to  make  representations  in  response  to  the  LOMs  and  have  made representations  to  the  SFC.    The  SFC  is  carefully  considering  these  representations. Meanwhile, no Licensing Condition will be imposed until the SFC has made a final decision regarding the intermediaries' eligibility as sponsors.

During this time, these intermediaries may continue to carry out sponsor/compliance adviser work and/or accept new sponsor/compliance adviser work.  However, they should consider carefully  before  accepting  such  work.  As  licensed  intermediaries,  they  should  contemplate whether  they  would  be  able  to  provide  proper  service  to  their  clients  and  act  in  the  best interest of these clients given the circumstances and the possibility that they ultimately may not be able to act as sponsors. In view of this inherent uncertainty, undertaking new sponsor or compliance adviser work by these intermediaries at this time may raise the issue of their ability to control business risk and in general, their overall fitness and properness as licensed intermediaries.

In the interest of their clients, intermediaries that have received LOMs should explain to their clients their latest status, and the possible implications arising from the course of action taken by them in response to the LOMs.

For more information on the Sponsor Guidelines and the sponsor regime, please refer to the Frequently  Asked  Questions 3 on  the  SFC  website.    Should  you  have  any  queries,  please contact your responsible Intermediaries Relationship Manager.
